sentences.text:
The accused persons are said to be (i) Arunesh Sita,
(ii) Balchand Chaurasia, (iii) Shyam Sunder Seth, (iv) Shankar Ram, (v) Parasnath Sharma, (vi) Anil Kumar Trivedi and (vii) Manjrul Kadri.

It is stated that the learned court below has issued processes under Sections 82 and 83 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against them vide order dated 04.10.2018 and vide order dated 22.07.2018, the learned C.J.M., Aurangabad has directed to produce the accused persons before him.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner and witnesses of Aurangabad P.S.
Case No. 120 of 2018 are the investors in the accused company.

It is alleged that the Investigating Officer of the case is not taking any interest in the investigation, he is not executing the order of the court below and from his inaction it appears that he has gone in collusion with the accused persons.
5.

In Cr.W.J.C. No. 752 of 2023, the petitioner claims that he is a poor investor of the company and has been cheated by the accused persons by alluring him to invest in the company in the name of some attractive schemes.

The case lodged by the Patna High Court CR. WJC No.1213 of 2023(3)
dt.16-01-2024 petitioner has given rise to Aurangabad P.S. case No. 119 of 2018 for the offences registered under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 469, 470, 471, 323, 504, 506 and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code read with of Section 3 of the Bihar Protection of Interests of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) B.P.I.D. Act, 2002.

sentences.text: The petitioner is praying for a direction to the respondent authorities to arrest the accused persons.
6. A counter affidavit has been filed in Cr.W.J.C. No. 1213 of 2023.
From the statements made therein it would appear that in fact the investigation of the cases have not progressed.

Only recently,
the Sub-Divisional Police Officer, Aurangabad has vide his Letter No. 149/Sadar dated 08.01.2024 submitted a report.

The case has been found true against (i) Arunesh Sita, (ii) Rasid Kanwar, (iii)
Balchand Chaurasia, (iv) Anil Kumar Trivedi, (v) Prince Rana, (vi) Parth Sarthi Adhikari, (vii)
Parasnath Sharma,
(viii) Shyam Sunder Seth and (ix) Manjrul Kadri, [all the Directors of (i) Indus Ware Industries Limited, (ii) Sakshi Mutual Benefit Trust India, (iii) Indus Broker House Private Limited and (iv)
Sun Rise Asian Limited] and (x) Shankar Ram under Sections 420, 406, 467 and other allied Sections of the Indian Penal Code.
Section 3 of the Bihar Protection of Interests of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) B.P.I.D. Act, 2002 Act has also been added.

sentences.text: It appears from the counter affidavit that process under Patna High Court CR. WJC No.1213 of 2023(3) dt.16-01-2024 Section 83 Cr.P.C. has been issued against (i) Arunesh Sita and (ii) Shankar Ram.
Production warrant was issued against accused Prince Rana and the same was made available to A.S.P., Jabalpur.
Production warrant has also been issued against Arunesh Sita and Balchand Chaurasia who were confined in Varanasi Jail in connection with Chetganj P.S. Case No. 97 of 2019.
7. It further appears that for the laxity shown by the Investigating Officer of the case during investigation a show-cause has been issued to him vide Memo No. 28/LC dated 10.01.2024.

sentences.text:
Mr. Rajesh Ranjan, learned counsel appears for S.E.B.I. and submits that appropriate statutory actions have been taken in the matter and S.E.B.I. has imposed a fine of Rs. One Crore which has been reduced at appellate stage to Rs. Fifty Lakhs.
9.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case as also the materials placed before this Court, this Court is of the considered opinion that since the Investigating Officer of this case has shown laxity and errors have been found in performance of his duty in course of investigation for which a show-cause has been issued to him, the Investigating officer of this case be changed and a new competent officer be given charge of this case Patna High Court CR.

WJC No.1213 of 2023(3)
dt.16-01-2024 at the earliest.
The show-cause issued to the present Investigating Officer shall be proceeded with in accordance with law.

10. The process issued under Sections 82 and 83 Cr.P.C. be executed within a period of two weeks from today and the Investigating Officer of the case shall also execute the production warrant to produce the accused persons before the court.

11. So far as other accused persons are concerned, against whom the case has been found true, the I.O. shall take immediate efforts to nab the accused persons and produce them before the competent court unless they are otherwise protected by any order of a court of law.
12. The Superintendent of Police, Aurangabad shall keep on reviewing these matters at his end every month and shall ensure that investigation of the cases are completed within a reasonable period.
13. Both the applications stand disposed of accordingly.

(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J) Rishi/-
